tools.name: world_now
tools.description: Use when the user asks what is happening in the world right now and wants numbers they can trust and cite: Bitcoin and crypto market, currency exchange rates, earthquakes in the past hour, space weather, where the International Space Station is, and more. Every snapshot carries its public tick numbe

tools.name: fingerprint_text
tools.description: Use when the user wants to know whether two texts are exactly identical, or wants a fingerprint to compare a document against later. Returns the SHA-256 fingerprint of the exact text, and whether it matches an expected fingerprint if one is given. It does not store the text or prove when it was writ

tools.name: request_service
tools.description: Use when the person wants something none of these tools can do and says yes to passing the request on. Records only the request text they agree to send (no name or contact). Ask before calling it.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_service" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
